## Decision: λοῦσ’ at 7.296

λοῦσ’ is λοῦσα (1 sg., “I bathed”) or λοῦσε (3 sg., “she bathed”). I decided for λοῦσε. (1) The active aorist of λούω is
transitive; bathing oneself is the middle (λούομαι), so “I bathed” would need an active used reflexively, which the
verb does not otherwise do in this idiom. (2) The subject of the sentence is ἥ (295); ἔδωκεν, λοῦσ’, ἔδωκε are three
verbs joined by καὶ … καί, and the μοι of the first clause serves as the unexpressed object “me”; the Greek marks the
second verb’s subject as the same by saying nothing, whereas a change to “I” would normally be shown. (3) Context: the
whole sentence lists what Nausicaa did for him (food, wine, bath, clothes), in defence of her. The note now says both
readings are possible and gives these reasons; `l` and `i` follow. (The earlier draft’s ground, that “he bathes while she
gives the gifts”, is an argument from the story, not the grammar, and would put the two hands in one line without a word to say so.)

## Considered and refused

- **Unit 8 note “nearly repeat 245–246”**: the order differs (ἔνθα Καλυψὼ ναίει … vs. Ἄτλαντος θυγάτηρ, δολόεσσα Καλυψὼ ναίει …); “nearly” is honest. Kept.
- **Unit 0/34 “again”**: 302 note says “again marks a reply from a man to a man”; harmless and true of 298→302. Kept.
- **Unit 4/6 particles μέν (245), ἀλλά (248)**: cross-reference checked, true.
- **Unit 25 δείλετο “imperfect”**: tense of this once-attested form is uncertain (imperfect or aorist); the note’s “imperfect” is the usual reading and the translation is unaffected. Kept.
- **Unit 29 note “softens what he has just said”**: an interpretive remark, not a grammatical label; no contradiction with `l`/`i`. Kept.
- **Unit 42 (γε at 315), unit 46 (μέν at 318), unit 47 (περ at 322), unit 29 (τε)**: emphasis or correlative particles left unrendered in `l`; English cannot carry them without distortion, and the notes name τε where it matters. Not changed.
- **Unit 45 ἐς τόδ’ … αὔριον ἔς**: note’s “‘for this … for tomorrow’: τόδε points forward to the day” is defensible (the ὄφρα clause is parenthetical); the alternative reading (τόδε → the ὄφρα clause) gives the same English. Kept.
- **Unit 40 `l` “things done in due measure”**: “done” is supplied, but αἴσιμα πάντα with no verb needs it in English and `i` matches. Kept.
- **Unit 44 `i` “pleasing” for φίλον**: `l` keeps “dear”; `i` may move to natural English. Kept.
- **Unit 14 `l` “rejoiced, for me, my dear heart, ill-fated”**: word order follows Greek and coherence wins ties; `i` is clear. Kept.
- **Unit 9 `l` “she” for relative ἥ**: note says relative; the unit ends at a comma so `l`/`i` need a main clause; the note already states the parse. Kept.
- **Unit 50 “called him by name … the name that follows is Zeus’s”**: true (Ζεῦ πάτερ); “him” in `l` is the house rendering of ἐξονόμαζεν. Kept.
- **Unit 60 `l` “bored” / `i` “corded”**: follows the table row at 3.399 and the published 7.345. Kept.
- **Remembered English in `i`**: scanned every `i`; no phrase found that arrived fully formed and could not be rebuilt from the Greek (“sweet sleep let me go”, “came into view”, “put to bed” all follow the case relations and the published wording). No change.
- **Repeated lines (7.240, 250, 251, 257, 266, 268, 282, 302, 311, 334–339, 344, 345)**: compared with the packet: unit 0 and 34 whole-unit `l`/`i` identical to the published ones (the validator will enforce); line-inside repeats reuse the published wording as far as sentence allows. No change.

## Checked and found right (no change)

ὡς + ἄν + opt. parse and reading; δείλετο lemma, person and meaning (tense left open); κέων (κείω, desiderative, pres. part. masc. nom. sg.; agrees with note 57 and `l`/`i`); πλέον (impf. 1 sg. of πλέω, same form 3 pl., unaugmented; subject is “I” from ποντοπορεύων; the added πλείων reading is harmless); ἐρξέμεν as future infinitive (needed after ἔλποιο); all other novel entries (case, number, tense, mood, lemma, Attic equivalent) and the 20 broadened entries’ new readings (αὐτῇ 246, αὐτὸς 327, αὐτῆς 263, βασίλεια 241, γένοιτο 316, κεῖται 244, λαῶν 323, μένον 259, πατρὶ 316, πρώτην 301, ἐχέμεν 313, ἔμελλον 270, ὀπίσσω 326, τῇ 281, τῷ 326, ὄφρ’ 319, τήν 271/322, θεός 246) each match their line.

## Considered and refused

- **Re-cutting `t` at 309/310 and 311/314.** The two mid-phrase cuts above are faults of segmentation (unit 39 should end at κεχολῶσθαι·, unit 41 at μένων·), but `t` is not to be touched in review; English and notes were aligned to the `t` as it stands. A re-cut before ingest would make 39/40 and 41/42 end on their ano teleia and let the English read as whole clauses again; that is a decision for the person who owns segmentation.
- **κεῖται broaden, “ὁ μὲν ἐν νήσῳ κεῖται ’πάσχων’”**: odd Greek-in-quotes in an older segment of the entry; it belongs to an earlier part, not this one. Not changed.
- **Length of broadened entries (up to 1212 chars for ὡς)**: the <230 rule is met by every novel entry (longest 134); broadened entries grow by design (“old entry whole, then ` · ` and the new reading”); each new tail is under 230. Not shortened.
- **Unit 8 `i` “and on the tenth, dark night”**, unit 4 “Atlas’ / Atlas’s” between `l` and `i`: style only, no sense error. Kept.
- **Unit 20 note “and there was shelter besides”**: ἐπί as “besides/there” is defensible. Kept.
- **Unit 30 λοῦσε vs λοῦσα**: pass 1’s decision stands (grammatical grounds given in the note); pass 2 only made the gloss list both parses.
